review.decision: Bound full receipts, keep exact retired acceptance evidence, and handle cancellation on both sides of the persistence boundary.
review.notes: Use only private HOME, synthetic clock jumps, bounded fixture slots, injected sync/unlink failure and a fake Codex RPC peer. Check original replay and compatible new admissions as well as zero mutation.

cases.description: Stable receipt retention and retirement free capacity without reissuing old input.
cases.setup: Private spool with stable accepted and refused outcomes, pending and uncertain ids, a near-full committed backlog and simulated passage beyond the previous 24-hour window.
cases.action: Look up within extended retention, continue admissions through multiple aged windows, settle an in-flight request at capacity and retry retired, pending and unknown IDs.
cases.expected: Full receipts are reusable within retention; expired terminal metadata frees room, a retired acceptance blocks native and fallback replay, and unknown evidence is preserved.

cases.description: An interrupted retirement reconciles its exact receipt and keeps replay protection.
cases.setup: Private spool and fault-injected durable retirement of an aged stable acceptance.
cases.action: Fail after payload removal, on index deletion, on receipt unlink and after receipt unlink before its directory barrier. Reopen with the normal operations and admit a new ID.
cases.expected: Committed accepted evidence is never converted into new authority; exact tail is recoverable even when its index is absent; unrelated orphan and unknown remain.

cases.description: Cancellation boundaries distinguish no publication, definite no mutation and uncertainty after attempted mutation.
cases.setup: Private spool around the final Codex guard and a fake RPC peer observing wire mutations.
cases.action: Cancel before or during final publication checks, cancel or expire after publication and before wire mutation, exercise raw RPC deadline checks, and attempt a transport mutation that loses its outcome.
cases.expected: Pre-publication cancellation leaves no durable request; post-publication zero mutation records a reclaimable refusal; actual or ambiguous attempts remain unknown and non-retryable.
